summary.one_liner: Adala is a Python framework for building autonomous agents that learn and apply data-labeling and other data-processing skills from a ground-truth dataset.
summary.what_it_does: Adala lets you define an agent with one or more skills (such as classification, summarization, question answering, translation, or text generation) and an environment made from a ground-truth dataset. The agent can run learning iterations against a teacher runtime with an accuracy threshold, then apply its learned skills to new data. Runtimes are pluggable: the README shows OpenAI chat models and, via OpenRouter, Claude and other OpenAI-compatible LLMs. A single skill can be deployed across multiple runtimes, including a student/teacher setup. Output templates and labels can be configured per skill. The README also lists a Classification-with-chain-of-thought skill, an ontology creator, and a math-reasoning example on GSM8k. It is designed to be used as a library inside Python notebooks, including with pandas DataFrames.
use_cases: preprocessing and postprocessing dataframes with LLMs
inferring an ontology from text examples
how_to_run: Define a StaticEnvironment with a training DataFrame, a ClassificationSkill, and an Agent with runtimes (see Quickstart in README)
notable: Agents learn skills iteratively from a ground-truth dataset rather than relying on a fixed prompt
Student/teacher runtime architecture where one skill can run on multiple runtimes
Works with OpenAI-compatible LLMs such as Claude through OpenRouter
Designed to run natively in Python notebooks against large DataFrames
caveats: Requires an LLM API key (OpenAI by default, or OpenRouter for other models)
Several roadmap items are unchecked, including a REST API, command-line utility, and named entity recognition skill
README does not state a license
